title: Ex 2.5 #9 · Truth table for ∼(∼P ∨ ∼Q)
prompt: Build a truth table for $\sim (\sim P \vee \sim Q)$ and enter the truth value of the whole statement in each row.
answer_format: Four T/F values, one per row, top to bottom, like T F T T. Rows (P, Q) go TT, TF, FT, FF, as in the book. Helper columns are optional steps, like ~P : F F T T.
hints: Work from the inside out: columns for ∼P, ∼Q, then ∼P ∨ ∼Q, then negate.
The outer ∼ negates the whole disjunction, not just its first part.
solution: $\sim P$ is F F T T and $\sim Q$ is F T F T, so $\sim P \vee \sim Q$ is F T T T.
Negating gives T F F F, the same column as $P \wedge Q$.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).
